package_info.why_malicious: All versions of snakeyaml below 1.26 are vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack due to the lack of restrictions on YAML alias and anchor expansion. Attackers can submit specially crafted YAML files (YAML bombs) that, when parsed, cause exponential memory allocation, leading to java.lang.OutOfMemoryError and application crashes.

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a malicious YAML file containing deeply nested aliases (YAML bomb) to the application.
attack_chain.leads_to: YAML parser begins processing the file.

attack_chain.action: YAML parser (snakeyaml <1.26) recursively expands aliases and anchors, causing exponential memory allocation and object creation.
attack_chain.leads_to: System memory is rapidly exhausted.

attack_chain.leads_to: Service becomes unavailable (DoS achieved).

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor YAML parsing operations for excessive alias and anchor expansion or unusually deep nesting. Implement and enforce limits on alias and anchor expansion in YAML parsers. Detect and alert on java.lang.OutOfMemoryError exceptions during YAML processing. Scan incoming YAML files for patterns of repeated anchors and aliases, especially those that reference each other recursively or exponentially. Use static or dynamic analysis to identify YAML files with structures that could cause exponential expansion.
